nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$ be a modal formula. If both $\varphi$ and its negation $\neg\varphi$ are local consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $\bot$.
nodes.title: Contradiction yields falsity

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi \to \psi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $\Box\varphi \to \Box\psi$.
nodes.title: The monotonicity rule for necessity

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas. A modal formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the empty set of hypotheses in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ if and only if $\varphi$ is a theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Consequences of no hypotheses are the theorems

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. In the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\psi\}$ if and only if $\psi \to \varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: The deduction theorem for local modal consequence

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas. The local consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ form the least set of modal formulas that contains every member of $\Gamma$ and every theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ and is closed under modus ponens: whenever it contains $\varphi \to \psi$ and $\varphi$, it contains $\psi$.
nodes.title: Local consequence in a normal modal logic

nodes.summary:

The theorems of the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ form the least set of modal formulas that contains, for all modal formulas $\varphi$, $\psi$, $\chi$, the propositional axioms $\varphi 	o (\psi 	o \varphi)$, $(\varphi 	o (\psi 	o \chi)) 	o ((\varphi 	o \psi) 	o (\varphi 	o \chi))$ and $

nodes.title: Theorems of a normal modal logic

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas. If a modal formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then there is a finite set $\Delta \subseteq \Gamma$ such that $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Delta$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Compactness of local modal consequence

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\psi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\psi \to \varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: The deduction theorem for local modal consequence, forward direction

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas. For every modal formula $\varphi$, the formula $\varphi \to \varphi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Self-implication is a theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$, $\chi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi \to \psi$ and $\psi \to \chi$ are local consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $\varphi \to \chi$.
nodes.title: Hypothetical syllogism

nodes.summary: The set of extra axioms of the normal modal logic K is the empty set of modal formulas over a given type of atoms; that is, K adds no axioms to the propositional axioms and the distribution axiom.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of the modal logic K

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$, $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be sets of modal formulas with $\Gamma \subseteq \Delta$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Delta$ in $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of local consequence in the hypotheses

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'$ be sets of modal formulas. Every theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is a theorem of $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda'$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of theorems in the extra axioms

nodes.summary:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $
eg
eg\varphi$, where $
eg\psi$ abbreviates $\psi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Double-negation introduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma \cup \{\varphi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\neg\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, where $\neg\varphi$ abbreviates $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation introduction

nodes.summary: For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal logic K, the logic with no extra axioms.
nodes.title: Consistency of K

nodes.summary: For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal logic S4, whose extra axioms are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ and $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$.
nodes.title: Consistency of S4

nodes.summary:
For every type of atoms, $ ot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal logic S5, whose extra axioms are the formulas $\Box\varphi 	o \varphi$ and $\Diamond\varphi 	o \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $

eg\varphi$ and $
eg\psi$ abbreviates $\psi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Consistency of S5

nodes.summary: For every type of atoms, $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal logic T, whose extra axioms are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$.
nodes.title: Consistency of T

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas each of which is valid in the one-world Kripke model whose world sees itself and in which every atom is false. Then $\bot$ is not a theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Consistency of normal modal logics

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $\Gamma$ a set of hypotheses. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then every formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Ex falso quodlibet

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas each of which is a theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Local consequences of theorems are theorems

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $\Gamma$ a set of hypotheses and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\neg\varphi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Proof by contradiction

nodes.summary: The extra axioms of the modal logic S4 are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T) and $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$ (axiom 4), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of S4

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, write $\Diamond\varphi$ for $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$. The extra axioms of the modal logic S5 are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T) and $\Diamond\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$ (axiom 5), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of S5

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\Lambda$ a set of modal formulas each of which is valid in $M$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of a set $\Gamma$ of formulas in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ holds at every world of $M$ at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Local soundness

nodes.summary: The extra axioms of the modal logic T are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of T

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be sets of formulas such that every formula of $\Delta$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Delta$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of local consequence

nodes.summary: The accessibility relation of the one-world Kripke model, whose single world sees itself and at which every atom is false, is an equivalence relation.
nodes.title: The one-world model has an equivalence relation

nodes.summary: For any type of atoms, the one-world Kripke model has a single world, which sees itself, and every atom is false at that world.
nodes.title: The one-world Kripke model

nodes.summary: Every theorem of the modal logic K is valid in every Kripke model: if a formula $\varphi$ is derivable in K, then $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of K for Kripke models

nodes.summary: If the accessibility relation of a Kripke model $M$ is reflexive and transitive, then every formula derivable in the modal logic S4 is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of S4 for reflexive transitive Kripke models

nodes.summary: If the accessibility relation of a Kripke model $M$ is an equivalence relation, then every formula derivable in the modal logic S5 is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of S5 for Kripke models with an equivalence relation

nodes.summary: If the accessibility relation of a Kripke model $M$ is reflexive, then every formula derivable in the modal logic T is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of T for reflexive Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $M$ a Kripke model in which every formula of $\Lambda$ is valid. Then every formula derivable in $K \oplus \Lambda$ (from the propositional axioms, the distribution axiom and the members of $\Lambda$ by modus ponens and necessitation) is valid in $M$, that is, it holds at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of modal Hilbert systems for Kripke models

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
